01.r: Joins this scene to what goes before.

02.r: Jesus goes into the temple grounds.

04.r: The one who acts in the scene.

05.r: Marks his entry into the temple.

07.r: The whole temple area, courts included, where the trading went on.
07.n: This study renders ἱερόν 'temple' and keeps 'sanctuary' for ναός, the shrine itself. ἱερόν takes in the whole sacred precinct with its courts, which is why the BSB says 'temple courts'.

10.r: Joins his entry to his first action.

11.r: He forces the traders out of the temple area.
11.n: Abbott-Smith: 'to drive, cast or send out, to expel'. The verb is built from 'out' and 'throw', and here it is done to people.

12.r: Every trader, not some of them.

13.r: The article turns the participles that follow into a description of people: those selling and buying.
13.n: One article covers both participles, so sellers and buyers are treated as one group.

14.r: The traders who sold goods in the temple area.
14.n: Abbott-Smith gives the first sense as 'to exchange or barter', the second 'to sell', and lists this verse under the second.

16.r: The people buying from the traders.
16.n: Abbott-Smith derives the verb from ἀγορά, the market place, and gives the sense 'to buy in the market, purchase'. He lists this verse as a use without an object.

17.r: The trading was going on inside the temple area.

19.r: The temple precinct, named again to stress where the trade was.

22.r: The tables at which the changers did business.
22.n: Abbott-Smith gives first 'a table, dining-table'. The same word came to mean a money changer's table, and later a bank; English 'trapeze' and 'trapezium' come from it.

23.r: The article; 'of' comes from the genitive case of the noun that follows.

24.r: Men who exchanged one currency for another, for a fee.
24.n: Abbott-Smith derives the word from κόλλυβος, which he glosses 'a small coin, a rate of exchange'. The name therefore points to the fee or small coin charged for the exchange.

25.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'to turn down, turn over', as of soil, and 'to overturn, overthrow', the sense here. The Greek puts 'the tables of the money changers' before the verb, as the YLT keeps.

26.r: Adds the seats to the tables.

27.r: The particular seats of the dove sellers.

28.r: The seats the dove sellers sat on at their trade.
28.n: Abbott-Smith derives the word from κατά and ἕδρα, a seat, and gives 'a chair, seat'; he also records its use of teachers. English 'cathedral', the church that holds a bishop's chair, comes from it.

29.r: The article turns 'selling' into a description of people.

31.r: The doves that were on sale there.

32.r: Birds sold in the temple area, most likely for sacrifice.
32.n: That they were sold for sacrifice is a reasonable inference from where they were sold; the verse does not say so.

tr_note: The Textus Receptus reads ὁ Ἰησοῦς, 'the Jesus', and τὸ ἱερὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, 'the temple of God'. Our critical text lacks 'of God'; the KJV's 'the temple of God' follows the Textus Receptus, and the Geneva, DRC, ASV and YLT have 'of God' too. The added article before Jesus does not show in English.
